subject: english
question:
**Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.**

I thanked the stranger and told him that it was very kind of him to have helped me in my need.

options.text: “Thank him very much,” I said to the stranger. “How kind of him to have helped me in my need!”
“Thank you very much,” I said to the stranger. “It was kind of you to help him in his need.”
“Thank you very much,” I said to the stranger. “How kind of you to have helped me in my need!”
“Thank you very much,” I said to the stranger. “It was kind of him to have helped me in my need.”

solution:
The correct answer is: **“Thank you very much,” I said to the stranger. “How kind of you to have helped me in my need!” **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is an **in****direct **speech and we need to convert it into **direct **speech.
 
• When we change an indirect speech to a direct speech, we must follow these rules:
 
 
• An exclamatory sentence has a sign of exclamation after it which changes into a full stop in the indirect speech.
 
• The "full stop" in the indirect speech changes to Exclamation Point ( ! ) in the direct speech.
 
• The reported verb 'told' changes to 'said to' in the reporting speech part.
 
• To express the exclamatory phrase, "What! Oh! How!" are used. (Express surprise)
 
• The conjunction 'that' is replaced with inverted commas ("...") to show the direct speech part.
 
• A comma (,) is added after the direct speech part.
 
• The first word of the direct speech is in capital letter.
 
• The pronoun 'him' in the indirect part changes to '**you**' in the direct speech part.
 
 

Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

Hence, direct speech is - *“Thank you very much,” I said to the stranger. “How kind of you to have helped me in my need!” *
